title: Miss, hit and expiry
lesson: The application owns lookup, database read and cache fill. A hit avoids a source read, while expiration causes a later miss.
transcript: 0–8s: The caller asks the application for data. A cache miss causes a database read, cache fill and response. The TTL bar begins draining immediately when the entry is stored.
8.5–15.5s: A later request hits without a database read or TTL renewal. The bar keeps draining, the clock marks the approaching expiry, and the entry expires at 14.5s.
16–24s: A new request misses and repeats the source read and cache fill. The caller receives the result before the stage fades; the title remains at both loop boundaries.
corrections: Added topic title, caller label and TTL label.
The TTL bar now drains continuously from each fill, including across the hit, instead of remaining full until a late countdown.
Used the topic-local normalized encoder with deterministic first/last frames and two-thread limits.
limitations: Illustrative timing; no performance benchmark or recommended TTL.
No source writes or concurrency are shown; a hit or unexpired entry does not prove freshness.
